answers: How many call-site arguments are a local of the calling function?
183 arguments over 61 distinct local bindings, 37 distinct locals and 46 calling functions.
What does the binding statement read?

9 write a literal inside the caller (9 containers, 0 plain values); 0 read a module constant of the caller; 5 call another in-repo module; 0 call a module that is not in this repo; 7 call a method on a value the caller already holds; 15 call into the caller's own module; 0 read a file or walk the tree; 0 are an attribute on an imported module; 6 are a comprehension; 7 are computed in the caller.
How many are built in the calling function itself versus read from somewhere else?

44 of 61 are produced inside the caller (a literal, its own function, a method on a value it holds, or an expression); 5 are a population that lives elsewhere (a module constant of the caller, another in-repo module, or the disk); 7 are a parameter of the caller itself; 5 have no binding in the caller.
How many are not built at the site at all?
7 of 61 are a parameter of the calling function itself, so the local is one more hop up and not a value built at the site.
Which bindings are ambiguous because the name is assigned more than once?
5 bindings (61 sites) are assigned by more than one statement in the same function, so the published origin is the last assignment the parser saw.
Which dependency modules do the locals come from?
method_limits: a local's binding is taken from the innermost function whose body contains the call line, and only one hop is followed unless the right-hand side is a bare name aliased to another local (then up to 4 hops)
when the same name is assigned by more than one statement the origin published is the last assignment the parser saw, which is why the assignment count is published next to every row
an argument that is a parameter of the caller is not a local at all and is published under its own arm; the value it actually holds is supplied one hop further up and is not measured here

a module constant of the caller is published as that arm even though it may itself be a literal or a read; what the constant is is carried in origin_detail.what_the_constant_itself_is, but only one hop is priced
call sites are the ones E516 already enumerated (matched by callee name inside the module that defines the surface); a call through an alias of the surface is not in the population
whether a caller's expression really covers every branch is not measured here: this face answers where a value comes from, not whether the branch is guarded
